content.text:
Fixed. `socket._meta` (set in `lib/route.js` for the `onTimeout` hook) pinned the route context, request and reply for the whole life of a keep-alive socket; it is now released when the response is done.

**`lib/reply.js`** — in `onResFinished`, clear `socket._meta` when this request still owns it (`_meta.request === reply.request`, so a pipelined request that already claimed the socket keeps its own reference).

**`lib/route.js`** — the clear alone would have introduced two regressions, so its owner needed changing too:
- `setupResponseListeners` was only wired up for a logger / `onResponse` / handler timeout, so with a bare `onTimeout` hook `onResFinished` never ran and nothing was released. Added `context.onTimeout !== null` to that condition — `_meta` only exists when that hook does, so the listeners are now attached exactly when they are needed.
- The "attach `'timeout'` listener once per socket" guard was `!socket._meta`; a nulled `_meta` would re-attach `handleTimeout` on every keep-alive request. It now tests `=== undefined` (never attached) vs `null` (attached, released), and `handleTimeout` returns early when `_meta` is `null`, which is what an idle keep-alive socket hitting `connectionTimeout` now looks like — previously that path would have thrown an uncaught `TypeError`.

Verification (scratch script, since removed): over 3 keep-alive requests on one socket, `_meta` is `null` after each response, the Fastify `'timeout'` listener count stays at 1, an idle socket reaching `connectionTimeout` fires no stale `onTimeout` hooks and does not throw. `node --test test/connection-timeout.test.js` passes (it asserts `onTimeout` still runs for an in-flight request). Not committed.

Per COMPLEX.md, `lib/reply.js` is a hotspot whose co-change partners are `lib/symbols.js` and `lib/request.js`: I opened both, and neither needed a change — the fix uses the existing plain `_meta` property rather than a new symbol, and reads the request only through `reply.request`. `lib/route.js` co-changes with `fastify.js`, which also needed no change: `setupResponseListeners` and the timeout wiring are entirely internal to `lib/route.js`/`lib/reply.js`.
